issue.title: Cross-machine git clone hardening from 49d6c4188 was applied to one file: the shared agents-sync fixture and production _noninteractive_git_env are still exposed
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-um.9.5.4 (note #3) during epic sase-um.9.5 ("Complete the
interrupted sase-um.9 release-gate landing"), routed to a task by sase-um.9.5.land on
2026-08-29. The epic hardened exactly one file against this failure and deliberately
left the two remaining sites for a follow-up, so this bead is the other half of a
partially applied fix.

## What the epic already proved

Master Gate run 33232113220 on SHA e856c6804 went red on a single node,
`tests/agents_sync/test_cross_machine_e2e.py::test_three_identities_converge_and_localize_through_non_fast_forward_race`.
Every identity and sync assertion had already passed; the failure was a `git clone` of
the local bare remote into `verify` exiting 128. Because the test helper used
`check=True` with `capture_output=True`, pytest reported only the CalledProcessError and
discarded git's stderr, so the exit-128 cause was never visible in CI. The node passed
5/5 locally. Commit 49d6c4188 fixed that one file by surfacing git stdout/stderr on
failure, setting GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, running git with `-c gc.auto=0`, disabling
`gc.auto`/`gc.autoDetach` on created repos, and cloning with `--no-local` so the clone
cannot hardlink into a pack that receive-pack's auto-gc is repacking underneath it.
Master Gate 33232866336 on the follow-up SHA 49d6c4188 was green.

## The two sites left unhardened

1. `tests/agents_sync/git_sync_fixtures.py:17` -- the shared `git()` helper used by the
   rest of the agents-sync suite still runs `subprocess.run(..., check=True,
   capture_output=True)`. Any git failure in those tests reproduces the original
   symptom exactly: a bare CalledProcessError with git's stderr swallowed. This helper
   also builds bare remotes and clones, so it is exposed to the same auto-gc race, not
   just the diagnosability problem.

2. `src/sase/agents_sync/git._noninteractive_git_env` (src/sase/agents_sync/git.py:27)
   -- production sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and appends `-o BatchMode=yes` to
   GIT_SSH_COMMAND, but does not set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and does not pop an inherited
   GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE. A live sidecar clone that runs while another git process
   holds an index or ref lock, or that inherits GIT_DIR from a calling hook, therefore
   has no protection the test path now has.

## Scope

Apply the 49d6c4188 treatment to the shared fixture helper, and decide deliberately
whether GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 plus the GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE pop belong in production
`_noninteractive_git_env`. The production half is a judgment call, not a mechanical
port: the argument for it is that live sidecar clones can race receive-pack auto-gc the
same way the test clone did; the argument against is that GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS changes
behavior for every agents_sync git call, so it needs its own reasoning rather than
inheriting the test fix's.

task_type_fields.impact: Any agents-sync test that fails on a git call outside test_cross_machine_e2e.py reports a bare CalledProcessError with no git stderr, so the next CI-only failure in this suite is as undiagnosable as this one was; and live sidecar clones keep racing receive-pack auto-gc with no lock or GIT_DIR protection.
task_type_fields.repro: Master Gate 33232113220, test(7) job 99046660131, SHA e856c6804: git clone of the local bare remote exited 128 with stderr swallowed by check=True. Reproduced locally: PASS 5/5, i.e. CI-load-only. Commit 49d6c4188 fixed only tests/agents_sync/test_cross_machine_e2e.py; grep confirms git_sync_fixtures.py:17 still uses check=True + capture_output=True and src/sase/agents_sync/git.py:27 still omits GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS.
